items.title: Embedded arc surgery on a spanning surface

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Chapter 8, Definition 8.1, printed p. 79; the full 213-page book PDF was inspected.

items.title: Total linking is intersection with a spanning surface for a link

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: §8.A, printed pp. 200–203, linking and Seifert-form conventions; the link case is proved directly here by Alexander duality and local meridian intersection.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link, let $F$ be a compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $L$, and put $X=S^3\setminus L$. For each component $K_i$, let $\mu_i$ be the positive meridian, oriented as the boundary of a small normal disk so that a positive tangent to $K_i$ followed by the disk's positive basis gives the ambient orientation. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with the free abelian group on $[\mu_1],\ldots,[\mu_r]$. Define the total-linking homomorphism $\varphi:H_1(X;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$ by $\varphi(\sum_i m_i[\mu_i])=\sum_i m_i$. If a smooth oriented loop $J\subset X$ is transverse to the interior of $F$, define its signed intersection number $J\cdot F$ by counting $+1$ when $J$ crosses from the negative to the positive side of the oriented normal of $F$ and $-1$ for the reverse crossing. Then $J\cdot F=\varphi([J])$.

items.title: Seifert surfaces of the same link are connected by arc surgeries

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Chapter 8, Definition 8.1 and Theorem 8.2, printed pp. 79–81; the complete source section was inspected in the full 213-page book PDF.

items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $L$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link in the oriented $3$-sphere, and let $F_0,F_1$ be connected compact smooth oriented embedded surfaces with the same oriented boundary $L$. There is a finite sequence of such spanning surfaces from $F_0$ to $F_1$ in which each consecutive pair differs either by an ambient isotopy fixed on $L$ or by one embedded arc surgery or its reverse.

items.title: The positive-push Seifert pairing is well-defined for a link surface

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: §8.A, printed pp. 200–203: Seifert-pairing and linking conventions; the link-surface homology argument is proved here.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $L$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link in the oriented $3$-sphere, and let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $L$. For disjoint oriented embedded circles $C,D\subset S^3$, define $\operatorname{lk}(C,D)$ as the coefficient of the positive meridian of $D$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus D;\mathbb Z)$, and extend it bilinearly to finite integral sums of oriented circles. This linking number is symmetric on disjoint circle cycles. Every class of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ has a representative that is a finite integral sum of pairwise disjoint smooth oriented embedded circles in $F$. The positive push-off $x^+$ of such a representative is a sufficiently small copy in the positive normal direction determined by the ambient and surface orientations. For representatives $x$ and $y$, the sum of the pairwise linking numbers between $x^+$ and $y$ depends only on $[x]$ and $[y]$, is independent of the sufficiently small positive push-off level, and is bilinear. Hence it defines the positive-push Seifert pairing on $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$.

items.title: Seifert pairing and matrix of an oriented link

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Chapter 8, §8.A, printed pp. 79–83: Seifert-surface and pairing conventions; the full 213-page book PDF was inspected.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $L$, and let $g$ be its genus. The compact-surface normal form gives $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{2g+r-1}$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be a positive ambient frame whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent frame of $F$. For an ordered integral basis $a_1,\dots,a_m$, with $m=2g+r-1$, choose circle-cycle representatives on $F$ and let $a_i^+$ be a sufficiently small copy in the positive normal direction. For disjoint oriented embedded circles $C,D\subset S^3$, define $\operatorname{lk}(C,D)$ by $[C]=\operatorname{lk}(C,D)[\mu_D]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus D;\mathbb Z)$, where $\mu_D$ is the positive meridian whose oriented normal disk follows the positive tangent to $D$ in the ambient orientation; extend linking bilinearly to finite sums of such circles. Define the positive-push Seifert matrix by $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The link-surface pairing lemma proves this matrix is independent of the chosen cycle representatives and push-off level. The surface and basis remain part of the data; this definition asserts no link-only matrix invariance.

items.title: An arc surgery enlarges a link Seifert matrix by two rows and columns

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory
references.locator: Chapter 8, Theorem 8.4, printed pp. 81–82: Seifert matrices under embedded arc surgery; the link-matrix calculation is proved here.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $L$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link with $r$ components, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$, and let $F'$ be obtained by choosing an embedded solid cylinder $[0,1]\times D^2$ that meets $F$ exactly in its two end disks and lies on the same local side at both disks, then replacing those disks by the cylinder's lateral annulus with the compatible orientation. This surgery preserves $L$. Put $m=2g+r-1$, choose an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ represented away from the two end disks, and let $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix. The surviving classes of that basis extend by two classes to an integral basis of $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)$, and for some column vectors $x,y\in\mathbb Z^m$ and integer $z$, the new Seifert matrix is one of
$$\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&0\\0^T&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&1\\0^T&0&0\end{pmatrix}.$$

items.title: Knot Arf invariant from the Seifert form

references.title: R. Robertello, An Invariant of Knot Cobordism, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 18 (1965), 543–555
references.locator: §§3–5, pp. 546–552: Seifert quadratic form, Arf basis formula, and determinant expansion modulo (2,(1+t)^4); all seven scanned pages visually inspected.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and $F$ a connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$. The Seifert matrix $V$ defines a function on $H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)$ by
$$q_F([x])=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,x)\pmod2=x^TVx\pmod2,$$
where an integral lift of the mod-two homology class is used in the last expression. Its polarization is the mod-two intersection form. A symplectic basis is an ordered basis $(a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g)$ with $a_i\cdot b_j=\delta_{ij}$ and all other pairings zero. Define
$$\operatorname{Arf}(q_F)=\sum_{i=1}^g q_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)\pmod2.$$
The quadratic-enhancement lemma proves that this value is independent of symplectic basis; the S-equivalence and Conway bridge proves independence of $F$, so the resulting knot invariant is denoted $\operatorname{Arf}(K)$. For $g=0$ the empty sum is $0$.

items.title: Seifert matrices of a knot are S-equivalent
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, and let $F,F'$ be any connected compact smooth oriented spanning surfaces for $K$. For any ordered integral bases of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ and $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)$, the matrices of the positive-push Seifert pairing are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular congruences and the two rank-two elementary Seifert enlargements or their reverses.

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory

items.title: The Seifert form gives a quadratic enhancement and basis-independent Arf value

references.title: R. Robertello, An Invariant of Knot Cobordism, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 18 (1965), 543–555
references.locator: §§3–5, pp. 546–552: Seifert quadratic form, Arf basis formula, and determinant expansion modulo (2,(1+t)^4); all seven scanned pages visually inspected.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. For a knot Seifert surface $F$ with Seifert matrix $V$, the function $q_F(x)=x^TVx\pmod2$ is well-defined on $H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)$ and satisfies
$$q_F(x+y)=q_F(x)+q_F(y)+x\cdot_F y.$$
Its polarization is nondegenerate. For any symplectic basis $(a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g)$, the sum $\sum_iq_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)$ is independent of that basis. It is unchanged by either elementary Seifert enlargement, so it depends only on the knot.

items.title: The singular parameters of the Levine–Tristram form

references.title: Anthony Conway, The Levine–Tristram signature: a survey, Matrix Annals 2016 (arXiv:1903.04477)
references.locator: §2.1, printed pp. 3–4: Hermitian form and Alexander-root determinant relation; §2.4, printed p. 7: averaged signature at roots; complete 18-page PDF inspected.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be any connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$, let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix, and let $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$. The Hermitian matrix
$$H_\omega=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T$$
is singular if and only if the normalized knot Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$ vanishes at $\omega$.

items.title: Levine–Tristram Hermitian form and signature

references.title: Anthony Conway, The Levine–Tristram signature: a survey, Matrix Annals 2016 (arXiv:1903.04477)
references.locator: §2.1, printed pp. 3–4: Hermitian form convention; §2.4, printed p. 7: averaged signature at roots; complete 18-page PDF inspected.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface with oriented boundary $K$, let $V$ be the matrix of the Seifert pairing $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ in an ordered integral basis, and let $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$. Define the **Levine–Tristram Hermitian matrix** by
$$H_\omega(V)=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T.$$
It is Hermitian because $V$ is real and $\bar\omega=\omega^{-1}$. Its signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues, both counted with multiplicity and with zero eigenvalues omitted. When $\Delta_K(\omega)\ne0$, define $\sigma_\omega(K)$ to be this signature. At a root $\omega_0\ne1$ of $\Delta_K$, define $\sigma_{\omega_0}(K)$ to be the arithmetic mean of the two one-sided limits of $\sigma_{e^{i\theta}}(K)$ as $\theta$ approaches an argument of $\omega_0$ from below and above. The invariance and one-sided-existence lemmas justify treating these values as independent of the chosen surface and basis.

items.title: S-equivalence and Conway normalization

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Chapter 8, Definition 8.3 and Theorem 8.4, printed pp. 80–82: elementary enlargement and S-equivalence conventions; the full 213-page book PDF was inspected.

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Chapter 10, Definition 10.3, Proposition 10.4 and Theorem 10.7, printed pp. 105–108: Arf invariant and Conway coefficient conventions; the full 213-page book PDF was inspected.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. For an even-order integral matrix $V$ that is the Seifert matrix of a knot, **S-equivalence** means the equivalence relation generated by integral unimodular congruences $V\mapsto P^TVP$ with $\det P=\pm1$, where $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ and $z\in\mathbb Z$, and the two enlargements
$$E_0(V;x,y,z)=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&0\\0^T&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad E_1(V;x,y,z)=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&1\\0^T&0&0\end{pmatrix},$$
and their reverses. For an assignment $P$ of an integer polynomial in $z$ to each ambient-isotopy class of oriented links, call $P$ **Conway-normalized** when $P_U(z)=1$ for the unknot $U$ and
$$P_{L_+}(z)-P_{L_-}(z)=z\,P_{L_0}(z)$$
whenever the three oriented links agree outside one crossing ball and inside it are respectively the positive crossing, negative crossing, and orientation-compatible smoothing; positive means $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})>0$, where $v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under}$ are the projected oriented tangent vectors and $P$ is oriented so the viewing normal followed by a positive basis of $P$ is ambient-positive. The smoothing reconnects the four oriented half-arcs in the unique noncrossing way compatible with their directions. No existence of such an assignment is presupposed: the Seifert-determinant lemma constructs a unique assignment and denotes it by $\nabla_L(z)$. For a knot, let $\Delta_K^\#(t)$ be the unique associate of its Alexander polynomial satisfying $\Delta_K^\#(1)=1$ and $\Delta_K^\#(t^{-1})=\Delta_K^\#(t)$; existence and uniqueness follow from the Alexander-normalization corollary. Set $z=t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2}$, with $t^{1/2}$ a formal Laurent variable, and use $\Delta_K^\#(t)=\nabla_K(z)$ as the normalization convention.

items.title: Seifert determinant constructs the normalized Conway polynomial

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Chapter 8, Theorems 8.5–8.6, printed pp. 82–83: determinant invariance and skein characterization. The local Hopf chart below fixes the sign for the stated positive-push and crossing conventions; the all-links determinant uses the inverse variable on the first matrix.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Every nonempty smooth oriented link $L\subset S^3$ bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface. If $F$ is any such surface with Seifert matrix $V$, and $u$ is a formal Laurent variable, then
$$D_L(u)=\det(u^{-1}V-uV^T)$$
is independent of the surface and integral basis, belongs to $\mathbb Z[u-u^{-1}]$, equals $1$ for the unknot, and satisfies
$$D_{L_+}(u)-D_{L_-}(u)=(u-u^{-1})D_{L_0}(u)$$
for every oriented skein triple. Thus $D_L(u)=
abla_L(u-u^{-1})$ for the unique Conway polynomial normalized by $
abla_U=1$ and $
abla_+-
abla_-=z
abla_0$.

items.title: One-sided Levine–Tristram signature limits exist

references.title: Anthony Conway, The Levine–Tristram signature: a survey, Matrix Annals 2016 (arXiv:1903.04477)
references.locator: §2.1, printed pp. 3–4: Hermitian form convention; §2.4, printed p. 7: averaged signature at roots; complete 18-page PDF inspected.

items.statement: Assume the hypotheses and conventions of the Levine–Tristram form definition. At every root $\omega_0\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$ of $\Delta_K$, each one-sided limit of the nonroot signature as the parameter moves along the unit circle to $\omega_0$ exists and is an integer.

items.title: The Seifert determinant detects Arf parity near minus one

references.title: R. Robertello, An Invariant of Knot Cobordism, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 18 (1965), 543–555
references.locator: §§3–5, pp. 546–552: Seifert quadratic form, Arf basis formula, and determinant expansion modulo (2,(1+t)^4); all seven scanned pages visually inspected.

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Printed Chapter 10, Definition 10.3, Proposition 10.4 and Theorem 10.7, printed pp. 105–108; complete argument read in full-text PDF copy; publisher chapter record inspected.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot of genus $g$, let $V$ be a Seifert matrix in an integral symplectic basis, and let $\Delta_K^\#(t)$ be the unique symmetric Alexander normalization with $\Delta_K^\#(1)=1$. In the quotient ring $\mathbb F_2[t,t^{-1}]/(1+t)^4$,
$$\Delta_K^\#(t)=1+\operatorname{Arf}(K)\frac{(1+t)^2}{t}.$$

items.title: Seifert stabilization preserves the Levine–Tristram signature

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Chapter 8, Theorem 8.4, printed pp. 81–82: the rank-two elementary Seifert enlargements; the block-signature calculation is proved in this item.

references.title: Anthony Conway, The Levine–Tristram signature: a survey, Matrix Annals 2016 (arXiv:1903.04477)
references.locator: §2.1, printed pp. 3–4: Hermitian form convention; §2.4, printed p. 7: averaged signature at roots; complete 18-page PDF inspected.

items.statement: Assume full AC. For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$, changing an ordered basis by an integral unimodular congruence or changing a knot Seifert matrix by either elementary enlargement or reduction preserves the signature of $H_\omega$. Consequently, the nonroot Levine–Tristram signature and its one-sided-average value at every Alexander root are independent of the spanning surface and basis.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. The stable isometry class of the Seifert quadratic enhancement and its Arf value are independent of the spanning surface and integral symplectic basis of an oriented knot $K$. Stable isometry means isometry after orthogonally adjoining finitely many hyperbolic planes $q_H(s,t)=st$ on either side. Under the convention $\Delta_K(t)=
abla_K(t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2})$ with $\Delta_K(1)=1$, the coefficient $a_2(
abla_K)$ of $z^2$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{Arf}(K)\equiv a_2(
abla_K)\pmod2.$$

items.title: The Arf invariant is the second Conway coefficient modulo two

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 175, Springer (1997)
references.locator: Printed Chapter 10, Definition 10.3, Proposition 10.4 and Theorem 10.7, printed pp. 105–108; complete argument read in full-text PDF copy; publisher chapter record inspected.

items.statement:
Assume full AC and let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. With the normalized Conway polynomial $\nabla_K(z)=1+a_2(K)z^2+a_4(K)z^4+\cdots$ and the Seifert-form definition of $\operatorname{Arf}(K)$,
$$\operatorname{Arf}(K)=a_2(K)\pmod2.$$

title: Levine–Tristram signatures and the Arf invariant — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A primitive sixth root makes the trefoil Hermitian form singular

references.title: Anthony Conway, The Levine–Tristram signature: a survey, Matrix Annals 2016 (arXiv:1903.04477)
references.locator: §2.1, printed pp. 3–4: Hermitian form and singularity at Alexander roots; §2.4, printed p. 7: averaged signature convention; complete 18-page PDF inspected.

items.statement: Assume full AC. The false statement is: “For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$, the Levine–Tristram Hermitian matrix of every knot is nonsingular.” The positive trefoil matrix at a primitive sixth root is singular. At that root the nondegenerate signature calculation does not apply; the defined knot invariant is the one-sided-average value.

items.title: Trefoil and figure-eight Levine–Tristram and Arf calculations

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
references.locator: §6.2.3, Example 6.2.11 and Proposition 6.2.12, printed pp. 44–47: genus-one trefoil surface and Seifert matrix; complete 53-page PDF inspected.

references.title: R. Robertello, An Invariant of Knot Cobordism, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 18 (1965), 543–555
references.locator: §§3–5, pp. 546–552: Seifert quadratic form, Arf basis formula, and determinant expansion modulo (2,(1+t)^4); all seven scanned pages visually inspected.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Use the positive-push Seifert matrices
$$V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_F=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$$
for the positive trefoil and the figure-eight knot, respectively. At $\omega=-1$, their Levine–Tristram signatures are $-2$ and $0$. In the displayed symplectic bases both quadratic forms have $q(a)=q(b)=1$, so both Arf invariants are $1$. Their normalized Conway polynomials are $1+z^2$ and $1-z^2$, respectively.
